title: Daily Market Digest: September 13, 2026
subtitle: Markets Closed Today - Recap of Friday, September 11, 2026

sections.title: Market Pulse - Last Session Recap (Friday, Sept 11)

items.headline: U.S. Stocks Rebound Friday as Oil Prices Ease, Inflation Meets Expectations
items.summary: U.S. equities concluded the last trading week on a positive note, ending a four-day losing streak as investors reacted positively to a slight retreat in oil prices and an August inflation report that largely aligned with economists' forecasts. This data strengthened expectations for a Federal Reserve rate hike next week, contributing to a cautious yet positive sentiment.

items.headline: Dell Technologies Surges on AI Optimism
items.summary: Dell Technologies shares climbed 12.0% to a record close, as investors were reassured about robust data-center spending following Oracle's strong earnings report, particularly its AI cloud services.

items.headline: Hewlett Packard Enterprise Hits All-Time High
items.summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise reached an all-time closing high, gaining 12.4%, also benefiting from positive sentiment regarding data-center and AI infrastructure spending after Oracle's earnings.

items.headline: ACXP Leads Standout Gainers
items.summary: ACXP was a standout performer, surging 83.10% on Friday's session, although specific drivers for the significant move were not immediately clear.

items.headline: Cooper Companies Plunges on Weak Outlook
items.summary: Cooper Companies was the biggest S&P 500 loser for the week, down approximately 22.98%, after reporting weaker-than-expected quarterly revenue and reducing its full-year outlook.

items.headline: MiNK Therapeutics Experiences Deep Decline
items.summary: MiNK Therapeutics, Inc. saw a deep decline on heavy volume, tumbling 15.54%, possibly due to an earnings miss, downgrade, or sector rotation.

items.headline: FactSet Drops Amid Market Volatility
items.summary: FactSet experienced a significant drop, falling 14.02% over the course of the week, indicating broader pressure on the financial information provider.

items.headline: August CPI Report Fuels Fed Rate Hike Expectations
items.summary: The Consumer Price Index (CPI) for August showed a 0.4% increase month-over-month seasonally adjusted, and a 3.4% rise year-over-year. Crucially, core CPI, excluding volatile food and energy, accelerated to 0.3% month-on-month, slightly above consensus. This print, combined with elevated oil prices, solidified market expectations for a Federal Reserve rate hike next week, with over 85% probability priced in.

items.headline: Federal Reserve Poised for Rate Hike Amid Persistent Inflation and Rising Yields
items.summary: Economists widely anticipate a rate hike from the Federal Reserve at its upcoming meeting, driven by stubborn inflation readings and sharply rising Treasury yields. The 10-year Treasury yield climbed almost 20 basis points this week to nearly 5%, a three-year high, increasing borrowing costs and impacting rate-sensitive sectors.

items.headline: Tech and Industrials Lead Friday's Rally; Utilities Lag
items.summary: On Friday, Information Technology ($XLK) led sector gains with a 1.32% increase, followed by Industrials ($XLI) at 1.07% and Communication Services ($XLC) at 0.99%. Conversely, Utilities ($XLU) lagged the market, falling 0.31%, primarily pressured by higher Treasury yields which diminish the attractiveness of their stable dividend payouts.

items.headline: Oracle's Strong Earnings Boost Tech, Kroger Delivers Mixed Results
items.summary: Oracle's ($ORCL) earnings report, released Thursday after hours, proved a significant catalyst, showing 30% revenue growth and a strong backlog in AI cloud services, which boosted related tech stocks like Dell and HPE. Meanwhile, Kroger ($KR) reported Q2 results on Friday, with identical sales up 0.2% but lowered its full-year identical sales guidance, reflecting mixed consumer spending trends.
